main_body: White porcelain bathtub seen from above and the south: a rim ring around a blue water surface, a thin grey front wall, and small feet
top_band: Rim and water form the top. Rows 3-4 are a white and light-grey back rim (L 236 and 201). Rows 5-9 are blue water (L 139 for the back-edge shade, then L 180). Rows 10-11 are a white front rim (L 228). A step to grey follows at row 12.
evidence: The scan shows a back rim (rows 3-4), a water surface with a darker back-edge row (rows 5-9), and a white front lip (rows 10-11). Below it are grey wall rows 12-13 (L 201, 164) and brown feet at row 14. The inside of the opening is clearly visible as water, 5 rows tall, so the container requirement is met. The front wall is thin, at about 2-3 rows, but it is present and shaded darker than the lip, so this is not a top-down slab. The tub reads as a 3/4 piece. It is borderline because the top dominates the front face.

style.evidence: The piece has about 5-6 lightness steps: white, light grey, mid grey and a blue ramp of dark edge, mid and a highlight spot. The outline is a bluish-grey tint and the neutral dark-edge share is 0%, so it is not a near-black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 flat blocks. The median is 10 colours per tile, which matches the Beodeul median, though it is below the references' 17-20. The total of 10 colours is low, but the piece is small and smooth porcelain. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.
